adjudications.question: fr uses «connexion» for a sign-in while the same namespace uses it for a network connection (`mobile.setup.verification`: «La connexion n’est pas encore confirmée»). Acceptable or ambiguous?
adjudications.rationale: Acceptable, and the alternative is worse. The polysemy is pre-existing and namespace-wide, not introduced here: `mobile.setup.title_login` ships «L’accès téléphone nécessite une connexion Radient» for the sign-in sense and `mobile.setup.owner_missing` ships «rétablissez la connexion du compte propriétaire», also the sign-in sense. «Connexion» is the ordinary French UI word for sign-in (Se connecter / Connexion); «identification» would be a calque that gives one concept two names in the same CLI, which the fr guide forbids in spirit and the glossary invariant forbids outright. In these three strings the account phrase («au même compte Radient», «à cette connexion») disambiguates. Residual risk is confined to the bare title and is logged as FR-01.

adjudications.question: fr narrowed 'newer' to the superlative «la plus récente» in the title and the receipt, while es kept a comparative. Acceptable?
adjudications.rationale: Acceptable. (1) The referent is unique: `providers/account_successor.py` returns a successor only when exactly one enabled, non-dead same-account row exists, so 'the most recent sign-in of this device' and 'this device's newer sign-in' denote the same row in every reachable state. (2) French cannot mirror a bare comparative here without a comparison anchor: «une connexion plus récente de cet appareil» reads as an unfinished comparison, which is why the translator kept the comparative only in the body, where «au même compte Radient» supplies the anchor. (3) The es comparison in the flag is not a clean contrast — es's title and receipt are superlatives too (ES-01). Recorded as FR-02, no change requested.

findings.status: accepted for this lane — recommend a wording pass in the next fr wave (does not gate: 0 blocker / 0 major)
findings.string: L’accès téléphone doit être reconnecté à la connexion la plus récente de cet appareil
findings.issue: Two things compound in the bare title: the connect- root doubles («reconnecté à la connexion»), and because «connexion» also carries the network sense in this namespace, a reader who takes that sense reads «la connexion … de cet appareil» as a link/connection rather than as a stored sign-in. The same doubling is in the receipt («Accès téléphone reconnecté à la connexion la plus récente»).
findings.assessment: Meaning is not lost: the title is always painted with the remedy body («Une connexion plus récente au même compte Radient …»), which names the account and settles the sense, and the desktop renders it beside the run button. Severity minor, not major, because no reachable state produces the wrong action from it. If a later wave touches fr, «L’accès téléphone doit être rattaché à la connexion la plus récente de cet appareil» (or «… à la connexion Radient la plus récente …») removes the doubled root without changing the reference.

findings.string: … à la connexion la plus récente de cet appareil …
findings.issue: Superlative where the English is a comparative; recorded deliberately by the translator.
findings.assessment: Referent is unique (single live same-account successor), so the superlative is true wherever the string can render. Keeping the comparative in the body sentence is the right split.

findings.status: accepted — inherited, not this lane's defect
findings.issue: English '(credential {id})' becomes '(identifiant {id})'. French «identifiant» prototypically means an identifier / login name, so the parenthetical can be read as naming the account handle rather than the local credential row. `mobile.setup.account` ships the identical parenthetical, so this is the namespace's recorded call, not a new choice, and the glossary's fr rendering for credentials is «identifiants» (glossary §2, note 6).
findings.assessment: Glossary-compliant and internally consistent; leaving it alone is correct here. Worth a glossary-side note only if a future fr wave distinguishes a stored credential from an identifier.
